question: Assume today is 2026-10-24. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Ministry of Transportation and Communications' (Tourism Administration) monthly statistics on visitor arrivals and outbound departures (來臺旅客及國人出國人數).

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Taiwan (來臺旅客人次) during September 2026, as reported in the Tourism Administration (MOTC) monthly statistics of visitor arrivals and outbound departures; counted as arrival events (visits) of foreign/non-resident visitors entering Taiwan, not unique persons, and excluding out
target.publisher: Tourism Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications (Taiwan)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-10-24 cutoff, but the official September figure is typically published with a lag (often ~1 month), so it may not yet be released at cutoff; the estimate is for the first-reported figure. Working interpretation: arrival events (visits) of non-resident

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals can be anchored on the same month in prior years (September 2023, 2024, 2025) and on the most recent months published before cutoff (e.g., July/August 2026), applying the historical September-to-adjacent-month seasonal ratio and the year-over-year growth trend. Target = recent monthly level × seasonal factor × trend adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total visitor arrivals for September 2023, 2024, 2025; monthly totals for June, July, August 2026 (and 2025 comparators); the September/July-August seasonal ratio in recent years. Minimum: at least two prior Septembers plus the latest 2-3 months before cutoff.

methods.rationale: Uses the end-September 2026 YTD (6,175,000, p111) times an assumed September share (~9.9%). This is essentially the difference 6,175,000 − 5,564,858 ≈ 610k, but expressed as a share so the ±5k rounding of the YTD and seasonal variation are captured in a1's range. Shared dependency: p111 and p4 come from the same MOTC release, so this route is not independent of the monthly series.

Placeholder structural route: scales a September 2025 base by a YoY factor. The library's yoy_scaling needs a September 2025 target value and a signal series; only August/July 2025 comparators (p129, p130) are kept, so this method is illustrative of the intended September-to-September scaling and would be completed by direction b1. If the required September 2025 value is absent, code will drop it.

assumptions.name: September share of Jan–Sep cumulative arrivals
assumptions.rationale: September is a low-to-mid season month. Using the 2026 monthly series (p120–p126, p1) Jan–Aug totals ~5.56M and typical September levels ~600–620k, September is roughly 9.5–10.5% of the Jan–Sep cumulative; midpoint ~9.9%. Range reflects month-to-month variation and the ±5k rounding of the YTD anchor.
assumptions.applies_when: The end-September YTD (p111) is the anchor and September is a typical low-to-mid season month.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published September 2025/2024 share materially outside 9.3–10.5%, or evidence of an unusual September event.

September 2026 likely close to flat to slightly down given typhoon disruptions (p82–p86) and the August dip; midpoint ~0.99 with a range spanning -5% to +3%.

methods.label: m1

p111.role: Cumulative visitor arrivals to Taiwan Jan–Sep 2026 (YTD anchor)

a1.role: September share of the Jan–Sep cumulative

methods.rationale: Decomposes the end-September YTD anchor into the September month via a historical September share. Strongest single constraint because p111 is a near-final official YTD figure; main uncertainty is the share assumption and the ±5k rounding of the anchor. Shares lineage with the monthly series (p4 is embedded in p111), so it is not independent of m2.

methods.label: m2

p1.role: August 2026 total visitor arrivals (latest observed month)

a2.role: September-to-August seasonal ratio for total visitor arrivals

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed month (August 2026, 662,735) and applies a September-to-August seasonal ratio, which is the correct period bridge (the earlier version wrongly applied a September YoY factor to an August level). The ratio is a dimensionless seasonal factor, not a restatement of any kept point. Failure mode: an unusual September shock (typhoon, cross-strait policy) or an August base d

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: September share of the Jan–Sep cumulative arrivals
kept.rationale: September is a low-to-mid season month. With September 2026 implied near 610k against a ~6.175M Jan–Sep YTD, the share is close to 9.9%; the range covers month-to-month variation and the ±5k rounding of the YTD anchor.
kept.applies_when: The end-September YTD anchor (p111) is the correct cumulative and September 2026 is a normal-share month.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 was unusually weak or strong relative to the Jan–Sep total (e.g. a market-specific collapse or surge).

kept.name: September-to-August seasonal ratio for total visitor arrivals
kept.rationale: September typically runs below August in Taiwan inbound data (school term starts, fewer summer-family trips, typhoon exposure), while Mid-Autumn/Teachers' Day holidays add some inbound traffic. A ratio near 0.92 with a wide band reflects that September is a shoulder month.
kept.applies_when: August 2026 (p1) is a valid base and September 2026 follows a normal seasonal pattern.
kept.falsified_by: A September 2026 level at or above August (e.g. a large holiday-driven surge or an August typhoon that depressed the base).

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
